# Burnticker — settlement coverage

<!-- Generated by `node --import ./test/alias-hook.mjs scripts/burnticker-coverage-audit.mts --offline --write`. Do not edit by hand: change the sources, the taxonomy or the audit, then regenerate. -->

**The rule.** A coin settles on a primary source, checked by an independent second source for the same fact. The second source must be run by another operator on another domain. A coin can also settle on an adjudicated Polymarket market, read from its on-chain payout on Polygon. Prediction markets help people find events, and they can serve as an extra check where their terms allow it. Kalshi's terms allow neither use, so Kalshi is never an input.

Mode: offline (frozen fixtures, data as of 2026-10-13). Taxonomy: `config/burnticker/categories.json` (11 categories). The same matrix is served as JSON at `GET /api/burnticker/v1/coverage` and drawn on the trust page.

A **primary** is a first-party source adapter: kind attested-http or on-chain, tier 4 or better, launchable, not an aggregator, not declared cross-read-only, never Kalshi. An **independent cross-read** reads the same fact (`fact` in `config/burnticker/sources.json`) from another operator on another registrable domain. **Hit rate** = readings the source's schedule expected in the 90-day window that one read produced; **latency** = first sighting by the keeper minus the end of the period; **disagreement** = shared periods where the primary and its cross-read differ beyond the fact's tolerance.

The game settles on the first final score read (TheSportsDB, or the league's own feed or API-Sports), and on its on-chain settlement where Polymarket lists a moneyline market and no score source answers. Both coins burn once two sources agree on the final, or 12 hours after the first final if only one source answers. Every source that reads the game must agree, and a disagreement holds the burn until they do. |
| Matchup pair, for every game this season (`matchup-season`) | **settleable** | Two team coins follow their own teams. Each game settles on its on-chain payout or on TheSportsDB's final score. Every source that reads it must agree, and a game only TheSportsDB can read counts once its final score has stood for 12 hours. |

## What we cannot settle today

- **No first-party source at all:** World. Nothing in these categories settles on a primary reading; only Polymarket's yes/no markets can, where a tag maps.
- **Settled on a single official source (owner decision 2026-10-12):** Natural disasters (`usgs.quakes`, `usgs.quakenext`, `nhc.storms`, `nhc.hurricanes`, `nhc.next`, `spc.tornadoes`, `spc.tornadoday`, `nifc.acres`, `nifc.firesize`, `usgs.volcanoraise`, `usgs.volcanowarning`). Each settles on its publisher's own published data. A day the feed is unavailable is held, not counted.
- **Primary source without an independent cross-read:** Elections & Politics (`fedreg.finalRules`, `fedreg.eo`, `fec.reports`); Entertainment & Culture (`wiki.views`, `steam.players`); Companies (`edgar.8k`, `github.stars`, `github.releases`, `github.milestone`); Health (`openfda.approvals`). One operator's number cannot settle a coin on its own, so these feeds are refused at creation until a second operator's read of the same fact is configured.
- **Settled numbers (scalar rules) in:** Elections & Politics, Entertainment & Culture, Companies, Health, World. Polymarket is binary-only, so where no primary pair exists there is no settled number at all: index closes, rates and commodity settlements (Financial markets), daily temperatures and rainfall (Science, Space & Weather) and every other Kalshi strike ladder have no replacement today.
- **Elections and votes:** adjudicated-only. They settle on Polymarket's payout vector or not at all; no official results feed is configured.
- **One-shot markets** (one question that resolves once): Polymarket only. No primary source answers an arbitrary question.

## How to read this

- **Independent operator, not independent measurement.** FRED republishes BLS series; the pair catches a broken endpoint, a parser error or a tampered response, not an error in the BLS release itself. The same holds for any mirror.
- **Latency is n/a until the keeper has run.** One read carries one fetch time, not a publication history; the keeper's readings table records the first sighting of every reading, and the live audit uses it once a token reads the source.
- **Zero-filled counts read 100%.** A day without a flare or a launch is a reading of 0, so their hit rate measures the read, not the publisher.
- **Snapshots** (block heights, stars, players) have no publication schedule; their cross-read pairs only reads taken within minutes of each other, which the creation preflight does.
- **Kalshi** is excluded as a primary, as a cross-read and as a venue, whatever any config file says: its Developer Agreement and Data Terms forbid settling products on its data or redistributing it.
- offline: every dry run reads the source's frozen fixture and its window ends at that fixture's fetch time; Polymarket tags are taken from the taxonomy as written (the live run checks each on Gamma)

## Per league — team coins and matchups

No ESPN reads. A league's games come from its free official schedule (MLB StatsAPI, NHL api-web), else from TheSportsDB v2 under its commercial license (`BURNTICKER_THESPORTSDB_KEY`). The NBA's own feed is read first when it answers; it has answered HTTP 403 since 2026-10-12, so the NBA's games come from TheSportsDB and settle on the on-chain payout and TheSportsDB. Each game settles on **primary A**, its on-chain payout where a Polymarket moneyline market exists, else **primary B**, TheSportsDB's final.

Every source that reads a game must agree; that is a source check, and one operator attester still signs the reading. The on-chain payout and TheSportsDB confirm each other when both exist. The league's official feed is a further read where it is free. API-Sports (`BURNTICKER_APISPORTS_KEY`) is optional. By the owner's decision of 2026-10-14, a game with no Polymarket market and no league feed settles on TheSportsDB alone, once its final score has stood unchanged for 12 hours across re-reads.

By the owner's decision of 2026-10-16, a single-game coin (one team in one game, and both coins of two teams in one game) has one burn schedule: it burns once two sources agree on the final (TheSportsDB, the game's on-chain settlement, a league feed or API-Sports, each counted once), or 12 hours after the first final if only one source answers. Every source that reads the game must agree, and a disagreement holds the burn until they do; a game that was held, or released by hand, waits the 12 hours. A source that never answers does not delay it. The first-read time is kept in the keeper's status table, so a restart does not reset it. Team, season, series and champion coins keep the rules above.
